definicion.title: What are change management services?
definicion.description: Change management services are consulting and support processes that prepare an organization's people to adopt a new way of working (a system, a structure, or a strategy) and sustain it over time. They include readiness assessment, stakeholder management, communication, training, and adoption measurement. The goal isn't for the solution to be installed, but for it to be used.

services.title: Core change management services
services.description: The four pillars in the next section run through the whole process. These are the specific services that make it up; they can be engaged within a project or on their own.

items.title: Change readiness assessment
items.description: We measure how ready the organization is before starting: risk level, sources of potential resistance, leaders' capacity to sponsor the change, and past experience with similar projects.

items.title: Organizational impact analysis
items.description: We identify what changes for each area and role (processes, tools, responsibilities, and metrics) to plan the transition around real impacts, not assumptions.

items.title: Executive sponsorship and change agent network
items.description: We prepare senior leadership to lead the change visibly and build a network of internal agents who drive it in every area.

items.title: Resistance management
items.description: We spot early where resistance is and why, and address it with concrete actions per group before it stalls the project.

items.title: Continuous AI-driven adoption measurement
items.description: We track organizational climate and the adoption curve throughout the project with AI, to correct course in time instead of finding out in a survey at close.

items.title: Reinforcement and sustainability
items.description: After go-live we consolidate new habits with follow-up, usage metrics, and adjustments, so the organization doesn't slide back to the old way of working.

items.title: Stalled adoption recovery
items.description: When the system is already installed but the team works around it, we diagnose the cause and run a plan to recover adoption.

items.title: Generative AI adoption
items.description: Programs for senior management and teams to adopt generative AI with sound judgment, through Cyrrus Leadership Academy.

pillars.title: Four pillars, one adoption process
pillars.description: Our change management methodology isn't an add-on: it's embedded in our Strategy, Solution Selection, and Project Management services. That keeps change management aligned with your organization's vision and objectives.

items.title: Stakeholder management

items.title: Communication plan
items.description: We develop effective strategies to keep everyone involved informed and engaged at every stage.

items.title: Training plan

items.title: Climate management

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about change management

items.question: What do change management services include?
items.answer: Readiness assessment, organizational impact analysis, executive sponsorship, stakeholder and resistance management, a communication plan, a training plan, continuous adoption measurement, and reinforcement after go-live. They're built into the project from the start, though we also step in when adoption has already stalled.

items.question: When does change management work actually start?
items.answer: From day one of the project, not as a closing activity: it's embedded in the execution of Strategy, Solution Selection, and Project Management, not run as a separate service.

items.question: How do you measure whether the change is actually being adopted?
items.answer: We measure organizational climate and the adoption curve continuously with AI, not just with a survey at project close.

items.question: Is team training included?
items.answer: Yes, the training plan is one of the four pillars of the process. Our broader training programs, including generative AI adoption for senior management, live at Cyrrus Leadership Academy.

items.question: Can you help if the system is already installed but the team isn't using it?
items.answer: Yes. While the ideal approach is integrating change management from the start of the project, we also step in when adoption has already stalled, through stakeholder management, a communication plan, and organizational climate management.

items.question: Do you help with change management for ERP implementations?
items.answer: Yes. ERP adoption is the most common case: the system gets installed but the team keeps working around it. We build change management into the implementation from kickoff, not as a rescue after go-live.

items.question: How is this different from traditional change management?
items.answer: Traditional change management usually arrives as a separate consulting engagement, after the technology has already been decided. Ours is embedded in Strategy, Selection, and Project Management from the start, with continuous adoption measurement — not a satisfaction survey at close.
